<!-- Hey there. Thank you so much for improving NewPipe. Please take a moment to fill out the following suggestion on how to structure this PR description. Having roughly the same layout helps everyone considerably :)-->

#### What is it?
- [x] Bug fix (user facing)

#### Description of the changes in your PR
Some very small issues were fixed by this PR. 
- I don't like this thing https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/compare/dev...avently:small-fixes2?expand=1#diff-20e0b2ce67b307277c153b396fb79660R355  but making the height anything but wrap content makes red dot in progress bar misaligned on Android 4.4, see #4245. With default height progress bar has smaller touchable area but looks ok on old devices too.
- this thing https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/compare/dev...avently:small-fixes2?expand=1#diff-57eb59a31e38fed8f965fb4a544e3b9fR540 prevents freeze on 4.4. Looks like some devices have even less available size for storing bundle data than Google recommends, see #4230. Anyway, this is how it should work and I'm fine with it
- brightness will be saved in the place where it changes.

#### Fixes the following issue(s)
closes #4271 
closes #4253 
closes #4245 
closes #4230 
closes #4277 
closes #4143
closes #4294 
closes #4292 
closes #4322

#### Testing apk
find the testing apk somewhere in this page because it's changes often

#### Agreement
- [x] I carefully read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and agree to them.

I have something interesting today. After I initially made this https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/dev/app/src/main/java/org/schabi/newpipe/player/VideoPlayerImpl.java#L1492
I thought it's too complex thing to maintain but I didn't find another way. Make once right and you never need to touch this `black box`. But from time-to-time we see new issues related to this code. After I saw how much needed to be done in order to make my code working here #4255 I couldn't sit back and relax and started to search an alternative.

So I found a new (old) way of how player positioning should work. It doesn't need to have all these manual calculations. It just works (almost identical to 0.19.8).

I checked in portrait/landscape, vertical/non-verical videos, with/without cutout, on 4.4 (emulator), 9, 11 (emulator), on Android TV (only a little bit), in multiWindow mode. Maybe some bugs still present on real devices, can't say. 

It's not a `small fix` so it shouldn't be in this PR but since I started to work in that branch I left it as is. I can create a new PR with just this one commit if you want but this commit uses the changes from this PR anyway.

@blackbox87 since you're referring to custom feature of your OS I don't want to do something with it. It's not my use-case. You can make a PR if you want but note that it shouldn't be default behavior because 99% of users with hardware buttons don't use custom feature of your rom. So it can be selected from settings but not default.

> @blackbox87 since you're referring to custom feature of your OS I don't want to do something with it. It's not my use-case.

> but note that it shouldn't be default behavior because 99% of users with hardware buttons don't use custom feature of your rom

If the option was unique to a random custom ROM then I'd agree with you, but the option exists in LineageOS, ArrowOS, Resurrection Remix, Pixel Experience, AICP and many more. And NewPipe is used by a lot of people who use these ROMs because you don't have to have GAPPS installed, so I'm not sure where you've got that 99% figure from as that's likely nowhere near accurate.

The issue might not impact you or me, but there are people out there who are using the option. So why not fix it now so that someone else doesn't have to report it and then fix it with a solution similar to my own? It just doesn't make sense to me. Having said that your approach to fixing issues seems different than my own since I often test my changes against every relevant OS option that I can think of, but your approach seems to be that if an issue doesn't impact your personal use cases then people can deal with it or fix the issue themselves. And that's exactly why I had to submit my own PR to handle cutouts in the first place. But the difference between your PR and my own is that I tested my changes against a few ROMs on real hardware, so I covered more use cases and have fixes in place for the known issues.

Hardware buttons shouldn't be a factor because if you've got gesture navigation enabled then it'll activate a software navbar. And that navbar will always have a height that's greater than 0 until you enable the option to hide the pill.

> You can make a PR if you want

I won't submit another PR since I've already demonstrated the problem and shared a solution. Plus my existing PR already fixes the issue.

> And NewPipe is used by a lot of people who uses these ROMs because you don't have to have GAPPS installed

I always use custom ROM. Lineage is my favorite. It doesn't mean I use the feature you are talking about. I just don't need it. When Android 10 was released, users can use system-wide thin navigation bar which is (probably) better aproach since it supported by every app natively (because of automatic insets). Instead of this custom thing from custom ROMs. This is why I said about 99% people that will not use the custom gesture navigation.

> The issue might not impact you or me, but there are people out there who are using the option

> but your approach seems to be that if an issue doesn't impact your personal use cases then people can deal with it or fix the issue themselves

So what? There are 626 issues currently open and I don't see that you are trying to fix any of them except the bug that impacts your current use-case, isn't it? You're saying that (based on your words) I should make code, spend my time for free without any interest in it based on someone's use-cases? It's insane. It's not my app and I don't care about problems that exist in software (except the ones that caused by me or the ones that needs to be made for me by me). Hello, it's free and open source software that made by people who want to do something. Trying to blame such people (us) that they don't want to do what you want to receive is a nonsense.

For some reason even you (which is strange, because you are a dev) don't want to understand that other people have their lifes and they should pay money for things in their lifes (like a house, cars, family). And all of that takes some time.

> but your approach seems to be that if an issue doesn't impact your personal use cases then people can deal with it or fix the issue themselves

It's not actually true because I did only 20-30% of things I need, other things were made on response to requests from the people here. That's because I think that the requests were clever/useful enough for me to spend time on it. You can review the whole PR and to ensure that I'm saying the truth #2907. 

> But the difference between your PR and my own is that I tested my changes against a few ROMs on real hardware, so I covered more use cases and have fixes in place for the known issues.

I said this:
>I checked in portrait/landscape, vertical/non-verical videos, with/without cutout, on 4.4 (emulator), 9, 11 (emulator), on Android TV (only a little bit), in multiWindow mode. Maybe some bugs still present on real devices, can't say.

So what's the difference you're saying about?:)

> Hardware buttons shouldn't be a factor because if you've got gesture navigation enabled then it'll activate a software navbar. And that navbar will always have a height that's greater than 0 until you enable the option to hide the pill.

The problem with your approach that you never know that you need to adjust padding. So some device don't have nor custom gesture control, nor virtual buttons, they have only hardware buttons. And for all of them you'll adjust the padding which will make the app looking different on devices. Which will create a possibility for bugs in a feature because it will be harder to check and to maintain. But looks like you don't care which is not the case for me. I want to make something that will work for everyone. Yes, sometimes I don't know how to make it possible but I'm trying. And this PR about that: I made a universal solution for positioning the player that makes your PR unneeded and works on every device without dirty hacks.

Your words: https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/pull/4255#issuecomment-690615580
> I think it is a problem since it worked perfectly before the unified player was added. That's the only reason I'm still trying to fix this.
At the moment I can't say that I'm a fan of the unified player as it's introduced more issues than it solves.

In this PR I tried to make the situation better by removing possible place for bugs but you still don't like it. 

I already said that you did an excelent job and I really thinks so. I just found that we don't need to do so much things like we do. The situation is much simpler and doesn't require from us manual calculations. 

>I won't submit another PR since I've already demonstrated the problem and shared a solution. Plus my existing PR already fixes the issue.

It's your choice. You can submit the PR or not, it's not what I would ask from you because as I said it's free and open source software, you can do what you want. And even if you show a solution, it's your code and I don't want to support it in case of bugs that could be found in it in the future. Your code = your responsibility. So if you want you can submit it or not.

> Plus my existing PR already fixes the issue

And you really think that my old code + code from your PR should be used instead of this new universal & easy code from this PR? If so, why do you like this custom hell that was started from my initial wrong way of doing things?

> When Android 10 was released, users can use system-wide thin navigation bar which is (probably) better aproach since it supported by every app natively (because of automatic insets). Instead of this custom thing from custom ROMs. This is why I said about 99% people that will not use the custom gesture navigation.

LineageOS 17.1 has the same gesture navigation settings as AOSP, but it also includes this additional setting. And that setting has been ported to dozens of other custom ROMs. So no, you can't guarantee that 99% of people won't use it. But even if 99% of people didn't use it then you're basically telling the 1% that you don't care about them, despite a fix existing with no negative side effects.

> So what? There are 626 issues currently open and I don't see that you are trying to fix any of them except the bug that impacts your current use-case, isn't it?

I've previously contributed code to NewPipe Legacy, despite me not using it. And I only pushed a PR that fixes cutouts because it previously worked almost perfectly in v0.19.8 and you seemed unwilling to fix it until I did.

> You're saying that (based on your words) I should make code, spend my time for free without any interest in it based on someone's use-cases?

Well, every bit of code that I push I test across multiple devices. And I do that because unlike iOS you need to check that things behave correctly on a variety of devices with different flavours of Android. But what I'm saying is that if someone says "hey, there's an issue and here's a solution" then you should listen to them and either use their solution or come up with your own to fix the problem. Like yeah, it doesn't impact you personally, but it doesn't mean that the issue doesn't exist and can be ignored. It exists and there will be people who use the setting, whether you like it or not.

I don't have all of the time in the world to do whatever I want either, but when you originally reported the issue with my commit did I ever say that it's not a problem because I couldn't reproduce your issue? No. I investigated it further, found the problem, tested the fix and then shared it. The same goes for my PR that fixes the rotation issues.

At this point I don't expect you to use my fix, despite me already putting in the work to test it.

> So what's the difference you're saying about?:)

I tested with every possible relevant option on LineageOS 14.1, LineageOS 17.1 & Pixel Experience across 3 real devices (2 phones and 1 tablet) and a couple of emulators. And the difference is that I found an issue that I could reproduce across multiple ROMs, so I fixed it in my PR. But based off of what you've said it's clear that you don't want to fix it because you don't think the options important enough and it doesn't impact your personal use cases.

> The problem with your approach that you never know that you need to adjust padding. So some device don't have nor custom gesture control, nor virtual buttons, they have only hardware buttons.

Think about that. My patch only applies when the navbar mode is 2 and the height is 0. So how is the navbar mode going to get to 2 if the ROM doesn't support gesture controls due to the hardware navbar? And even if a custom ROM supported it then when you enable gesture controls the navbar height becomes the size of the pills mini navbar and not the devices actual navbar. And I know that because I've tested it already.

> And for all of them you'll adjust the padding which will make the app looking different on devices

If you apply 16dp in landscape and 4dp in portrait then it'll look correct on various devices as it scales up or down depending on your screen size and density. And even if the extra padding isn't perfect it's still an improvement as the current solution guarantees that NewPipe's seekbar is drawn directly over the hidden gesture bar.

> In this PR I tried to make the situation better by removing possible place for bugs but you still don't like it.
I already said that you did an excelent job and I really thinks so. I just found that we don't need to do so much things like we do. The situation is much simpler and doesn't require from us manual calculations.

To quote myself "[I'm happy with whatever as long as this gets fixed](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/pull/4154#issuecomment-687993427)". I just don't agree with ignoring problems, which my commit fixes.

> And you really think that my old code + code from your PR should be used instead of this new universal & easy code from this PR? If so, why do you like this custom hell that was started from my initial wrong way of doing things?

There's no question that your method is cleaner. I mean that's to be expected too since you're a lot more familiar with the code than me. But you can't deny that my version currently supports more use cases.

> despite a fix existing with no negative side effects

It is what you think but the reallity is not so easy. Someone may find a bug in this code or Android will change something in the future. You can't be sure. Even if this code will work ideal forever it's your code, you can make a PR with it or not, I don't want to push your code.

> And I only pushed a PR that fixes cutouts because it previously worked almost perfectly in v0.19.8 and you seemed unwilling to fix it until I did.

But it doesn't mean you're fixing all those 626 issues NewPipe has. And I shouldn't do it too. And non of your arguments can make me thinking that I should.

> But what I'm saying is that if someone says "hey, there's an issue and here's a solution" then you should listen to them and either use their solution or come up with your own to fix the problem

Disagree. Someone gives you a code saying that it fixes some issues you don't even care/know about and you're saying that you will automatically push it to the master? Oh, that's bad. Don't think it's a good situation.

> But based off of what you've said it's clear that you don't want to fix it because you don't think the options important enough and it doesn't impact your personal use cases.

I don't want to fix it because there is nothing to fix. Everything works as expected. If you have different vision, you can make a PR. That's it.

> Think about that. My patch only applies when the navbar mode is 2 and the height is 0.

Oh, wait. You know more information for YOUR code than me, hm, isn't it mean that you probably the best person who need to make a PR?:)

>  I just don't agree with ignoring problems, which my commit fixes.

Same for me. That's why you can find multiple PRs here when I fixed some problems with my code.

> But you can't deny that my version currently supports more use cases

The code you're asking to include doesn't rely on your changes, isn't it? So you can just paste it inside my approach. If it's not true than it means you're asking about adapting YOUR code to my code which will cost me some hours/days to figure out how to make it working universally.

> It is what you think but the reallity is not so easy. Someone may find a bug in this code or Android will change something in the future. You can't be sure. Even if this code will work ideal forever it's your code, you can make a PR with it or not, I don't want to push your code.
